ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle A=30^\circ$, and $BC=2$. Let $D$ be any point on $AC$, and let $F$ be the midpoint of $AB$. Draw line $BD$. Let $E$ be a point on $BD$ such that $CD^{2}=DE\cdot BD$. Draw line $EF$. What is the minimum value of $EF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In $\triangle CED$ and $\triangle BDC$,\\
$\because CD^2=DE\cdot BD$,\\
$\therefore \frac{CD}{DB}=\frac{DE}{DC}$,\\
$\because \angle EDC=\angle CDB$,\\
$\therefore \triangle CDE\sim \triangle BDC$,\\
$\therefore \angle DEC=\angle DCB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BEC=180^\circ-\angle DEC=90^\circ$,\\
As shown in the diagram, let Q be the midpoint of BC, then EQ= $\frac{1}{2}$ BC=1,\\
$\because \angle ACB=90^\circ$ and $\angle A=30^\circ$, BC=2,\\
$\therefore AB=2BC=4$,\\
$\therefore AC= \sqrt{AB^2-BC^2}=\sqrt{4^2-2^2}=2\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\because F$ is the midpoint of AB, and Q is the midpoint of BC,\\
$\therefore FQ= \frac{1}{2} AC= \sqrt{3}$,\\
$\because EF\geq FQ-EQ$, when and only when points E, F, and Q are collinear, EF can reach $\sqrt{3}-1$,\\
$\therefore The minimum value of EF is \boxed{\sqrt{3}-1}$.

method.method_draft: Coordinate optimization method. Read the figure as a right triangle with C at the right-angle corner, AC vertical, BC horizontal, D on AC, E on BD, and F the midpoint of AB. From the text, set coordinates C=(0,0), B=(-2,0), and because the triangle is 30-60-90 with BC=2, take A=(0,2√3). Then F, the midpoint of AB, is F=(-1,√3). Let D=(0,t), where 0≤t≤2√3. Since BD=√(t^2+4) and CD=t, the condition CD^2=DE·BD gives DE/BD=t^2/(t^2+4). Because E lies on BD from D toward B, the section formula gives E=D+(t^2/(t^2+4))(B−D)=(-2t^2/(t^2+4), 4t/(t^2+4)). Compute EF^2=[(4−t^2)/(t^2+4)]^2+[4t/(t^2+4)−√3]^2, which simplifies to EF^2=4−8√3·t/(t^2+4). Thus minimizing EF is equivalent to maximizing t/(t^2+4) on 0≤t≤2√3. Its derivative is (4−t^2)/(t^2+4)^2, so the maximum occurs at t=2. Then EF^2=4−2√3=(√3−1)^2, so the minimum is √3−1.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle A=30^\circ$, and $BC=2$. Let $D$ be any point on $AC$, and let $F$ be the midpoint of $AB$. Draw line $BD$. Let $E$ be a point on $BD$ such that $CD^{2}=DE\cdot BD$. Draw line $EF$. What is the minimum value of $EF$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} In $\triangle CED$ and $\triangle BDC$,\\
$\because CD^2=DE\cdot BD$,\\
$\therefore \frac{CD}{DB}=\frac{DE}{DC}$,\\
$\because \angle EDC=\angle CDB$,\\
$\therefore \triangle CDE\sim \triangle BDC$,\\
$\therefore \angle DEC=\angle DCB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BEC=180^\circ-\angle DEC=90^\circ$,\\
As shown in the diagram, let Q be the midpoint of BC, then EQ=$\frac{1}{2}$BC=1,\\
$\because \angle ACB=90^\circ$ and $\angle A=30^\circ$, BC=2,\\
$\therefore AB=2BC=4$,\\
$\therefore AC=\sqrt{AB^2-BC^2}=\sqrt{4^2-2^2}=2\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\because F$ is the midpoint of AB, and Q is the midpoint of BC,\\
$\therefore FQ=\frac{1}{2}AC=\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\because EF\geq FQ-EQ$, when and only when points E, F, and Q are collinear, EF can reach $\sqrt{3}-1$,\\
$\therefore$ The minimum value of $EF$ is $\boxed{\sqrt{3}-1}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In triangle ABC in the figure, A is at the upper right, C is at the lower right, and B is at the lower left; AC is vertical, BC is horizontal, so ∠ACB is a right angle. Point D is on AC, point F is on AB, line segment BD has been drawn, point E is located on BD, and EF has been connected.

Then reason: From the given condition CD^2=DE·BD, it can be written as CD/DB=DE/DC. Also because E, D, B are collinear, ∠EDC and ∠CDB are the same included angle, therefore △CDE∼△BDC. Thus ∠DEC=∠DCB=90°, so CE⊥BE, that is, ∠BEC=90°. Therefore, as D changes, E is on the circle with BC as diameter.

Let Q be the midpoint of BC, then Q is the center of this circle, and EQ=BC/2=1. Also ∠ACB=90°, ∠A=30°, BC=2, so △ABC is a 30°-60°-90° triangle, AB=2BC=4, AC=√(AB^2-BC^2)=√(16-4)=2√3.

F is the midpoint of AB, and Q is the midpoint of BC, so FQ is the midline of △ABC, FQ=AC/2=√3. Point E is on the circle centered at Q with radius 1, therefore the minimum value of EF is the shortest distance from point F to this circle, namely FQ−EQ=√3−1. Equality is attained when the three points E, Q, F are collinear and E is on the circle near F.
